segments.say: Lesson 22. Guardrails, Safety & Prompt Injection. Input/output filters, P I I redaction, prompt-injection defense and least-privilege tools. Basics every A I engineer is asked about.

Guardrails are checks around an L L M app that block harmful inputs and outputs, protect private data, and limit what an agent can do, so mistakes or attacks can't cause real damage. Here is an analogy. The safety systems around a powerful machine: guards on the input, a stop button, sensors on the output, and the operator only allowed to press certain buttons.

Why does this matter? Every production L L M app needs basic protections; interviewers expect you to mention them. A few key words. Prompt injection: Text that tries to override the app's instructions. Indirect injection: Malicious instructions hidden in documents or web pages. P I I: Personally identifiable information. Least privilege: Give tools only the access they truly need.

segments.sec: Watch: Defense in depth around an LLM app
segments.say: Defense in depth around an L L M app. Treat all input as untrusted: user text, retrieved documents, emails, web pages and tool outputs.

segments.sec: Watch: Defense in depth around an LLM app
segments.say: Input guards: redact P I I, detect jailbreak or injection attempts, block off-topic requests (for example classifiers, Llama Guard, Presidio).

segments.sec: Watch: Defense in depth around an LLM app
segments.say: Indirect prompt injection: a retrieved doc contains hidden instructions. Delimit data clearly and tell the model that content inside tags is data, never instructions.

segments.sec: Watch: Defense in depth around an LLM app
segments.say: Limit the blast radius: least-privilege tools, read-only by default, scoped credentials, human approval for destructive actions.

segments.sec: Watch: Defense in depth around an LLM app
segments.say: Output guards: validate the schema, scan for P I I or secrets, check groundedness, enforce policy.

segments.sec: Watch: Defense in depth around an LLM app
segments.say: Pass leads to respond. Fail leads to safe fallback, log and alert. No single layer is perfect, hence defense in depth.

Main risks (O W A S P Top 10 for L L M apps, condensed). Prompt injection, direct and indirect. Sensitive information disclosure (P I I, secrets, system prompt leakage). Excessive agency: tools with too much power. Improper output handling: executing model output as code or sequel without validation. Data and model poisoning, unbounded consumption (cost DoS), misinformation.

Practical controls. Input/output classifiers and allow-lists. Structured outputs with validation. Never put secrets in prompts. Parameterize sequel, sandbox code execution. Rate limits and per-user token budgets. Permission-aware retrieval (users only retrieve what they can access). Red-teaming plus safety evals in C I. Tools: Guardrails A I, NeMo Guardrails, Llama Guard, Presidio.

Say it in the interview. "I assume prompt injection can't be fully prevented, so I limit impact: treat all retrieved and tool content as untrusted data, use least-privilege scoped tools with human approval for writes, validate outputs before acting, redact P I I, enforce rate and token limits, and run red-team evals in C I.".

Let's compare. Direct injection: "Ignore your rules and. ", input classifier, robust system prompt. Indirect injection: instructions hidden in a web page or doc, delimit data, least privilege, output checks. Data leakage: model reveals other users' data, permission-aware retrieval, P I I filters. Excessive agency: agent deletes prod D B, scoped tools, approval gates. Cost abuse: huge prompts in a loop, rate limits, max tokens, budgets.

A likely interview question: How do you defend against prompt injection? A strong answer: Defense in depth: treat external content as data with clear delimiters, input and output classifiers, least-privilege tools, human approval for risky actions, validated outputs before execution, monitoring and red-team evals. Assume some injections will get through and limit the blast radius.
That's it for Guardrails, Safety & Prompt Injection. Now play the quiz and games in the app to lock it in. See you in the next lesson.
